Virus injection in the dorsal raphe nucleus. Injection is performed with an angled approach (32°), in six different points (black circles) around the target (blue circle). We observed that the viral spread within the DRN is low (when compared with other brain areas), thus we use six points of injection to guarantee a wider spread of the viral particles within the DRN. Optical fiber implantation Mount the fiber on the stereotaxic holder in the right arm. Position the fiber tip on bregma and calculate target coordinates. Remove wet sponge from the craniotomy and keep it wet with saline ( Figure 3A ). In case of additional check for exact fiber location (see Data analysis section), apply a fluorescent dye ( e.g ., DiI) to the fiber sides before implantation, using a syringe with a 30 G needle (be careful and do not cover the tip of the fiber). Move the right arm to the anterior-posterior target position ( Figure 3B ). Insert the fiber slowly into the dorsal-ventral position ( Figure 3C ). For optogenetic experiments (not for fiber photometry) a 180 μm retraction along the dorsal-ventral axis is recommended for the final target. Note: Before reaching the final target, apply eye ointment in the craniotomy (just enough to cover the space between the fiber and the skull). Alternatively, agarose gel (1%, 10 mg in 1 ml water, Sigma-Aldrich) can be used to cover the craniotomy. Figure

Recipes Super bond C&B Use the super bond kit to prepare one small spoon of polymer L-type clear, four drops of monomer and one drop of catalyst. Stir gently and apply immediately (< 2 min) using the brush. It is very important to apply the super bond immediately after preparation. Keep the dispensing dish at 4 °C before using (recommended temperature range of the dish is 10-16 °C) and clean it immediately after usage.

steps.title: Setup stereotaxic surgery station
steps.instruction: Arrange the stereotaxic frame with a gas anesthesia system on a surgery table, place a heating pad covered by a surgical drape beneath the mouse mask, locate the picospritzer on a nearby shelf, attach the microscope to the wall, and keep all required materials (including dental drill) within reach.

steps.title: Prepare glass pipette and virus
steps.instruction: Pull a quartz glass pipette, mark three positions (upper and lower limits of 1 µl total volume – 5.9 mm apart – and a midpoint), fill the pipette with virus (10¹³ GC/ml) using a suction tool, place the pipette in a Petri dish, cover with Parafilm and store in the fridge.

steps.title: Prepare heating pad and saline bath
steps.instruction: Turn on the heating pad and set it to 37 °C. Prepare a 25 ml glass beaker with 10 ml sterile 0.9 % NaCl saline and add small pieces of absorbable sponges.

steps.title: Anesthetize and position mouse
steps.instruction: Weigh the mouse, place it in the isoflurane induction chamber (4 % isoflurane at 1 L/min), then move it to the anesthesia mask, fix it on the heating pad, secure it in the stereotaxic frame, and adjust isoflurane to 0.5‑1 % while monitoring breathing.

substeps.instruction: Confirm anesthesia by lack of response to a toe pinch; repeat the toe‑pinch test every 20 min during surgery.

steps.title: Administer analgesics and local anesthetic
steps.instruction: Inject analgesic Dolorex (10 mg/ml) diluted 1:20 in saline at 0.1 ml per 25 g body weight subcutaneously, then inject 0.1 ml lidocaine (2 % = 20 mg/ml) under the scalp for local analgesia.

steps.title: Clean scalp and protect eyes
steps.instruction: Shave the head from the eyes to behind the ears, clean the skin sequentially with a cotton swab dipped in betadine, distilled water, and betadine again, then apply eye ointment (e.g., Vidisic, 2 mg/ml) and cover the eyes.

steps.title: Make scalp incision and expose skull
steps.instruction: Make a midline incision from anterior to posterior (between the eyes to the back of the skull), swab the incision with saline‑dipped cotton, scrape away tissue with a bone scraper, and clean the exposed skull with distilled‑water‑dipped cotton.

substeps.instruction: Optionally use a Colibri retractor to improve exposure.

steps.title: Align skull and mark bregma
steps.instruction: If using zygomatic ear cups, align the skull flat in the anterior‑posterior and medial‑lateral axes using two needles mounted on the left arm; if using ear bars, align only the anterior‑posterior (bregma‑lambda) axis, then estimate and mark the bregma location.

substeps.instruction: Ensure the skull is clean, dry, and free of blood or fur; use a dry cotton swab to absorb any liquid.
Make thin cuts in the bone with a scalpel to improve Super Bond adhesion and dry the skull with a compressed‑air duster.

steps.title: Apply Super Bond to skull
steps.instruction: Retrieve the Super Bond C&B container from the fridge, prepare the mixture (see recipe), and apply a thin layer over the skull with a brush, leaving the bregma mark exposed and avoiding any skin contact.

substeps.instruction: Work quickly (C9‑C10); if Super Bond contacts skin, remove it immediately with forceps.

steps.title: Calculate angled target coordinates
steps.instruction: Mount a needle on the right arm set at a 32° angle, mark bregma, and compute the corrected target coordinates for the dorsal raphe nucleus (DRN) using:

substeps.instruction: xf = xB + xt + zt × tan α
where DRN target: AP = ‑4.7 mm, DV = ‑2.9 mm; α = 32°.

steps.title: Drill craniotomy and remove dura
steps.instruction: Drill a craniotomy around the calculated target mark through the Super Bond layer, then remove the dura with a 30 G needle; if bleeding occurs, clean with a cotton swab and apply an absorbable sponge, finally cover the opening with a wet saline‑soaked sponge.

steps.title: Load virus pipette and position
steps.instruction: Mount the virus‑filled pipette on the stereotaxic holder in the right arm, bring the pipette tip to bregma to verify coordinates, remove the wet sponge from the craniotomy, and move the right arm to the target anterior‑posterior position before penetrating the brain.

steps.title: Inject virus at six sites
steps.instruction: Set the picospritzer to a 2000 msec period and 1.0 msec pulse duration, then inject the virus at six locations: two anterior‑posterior positions (100 µm anterior and 100 µm posterior to the target) each combined with three dorsal‑ventral depths (100 µm above, at, and 100 µm below the target), delivering approximately one‑sixth of the total viral volume per point.

substeps.instruction: Wait 5 min between removing the pipette from each anterior‑posterior location.
After all injections, raise the arm.

steps.title: Optional: Prepare fiber cannula
steps.instruction: If a fiber cannula will be implanted, keep the right arm in place, replace the stereotaxic holder with the cannula fiber holder, and keep the craniotomy covered with a wet saline‑soaked sponge.

steps.title: Implant optical fiber
steps.instruction: Mount the optical fiber on the right‑arm holder, position the fiber tip at bregma to recalculate target coordinates, optionally apply DiI dye to the fiber sides with a 30 G syringe (avoid covering the tip), move to the anterior‑posterior target, and slowly lower the fiber to the dorsal‑ventral target.

substeps.instruction: For optogenetic experiments (not fiber photometry) retract the fiber 180 µm dorsally‑ventrally from the final target.
Before reaching the final depth, apply a thin layer of eye ointment in the craniotomy or cover the opening with 1 % agarose gel (10 mg in 1 ml water).

steps.title: Secure implant with dental acrylic
steps.instruction: Apply dental acrylic in small increments until the fiber (or cannula) is firmly fixed to the skull; once the acrylic is dry and hard, remove any sharp edges with a drill if necessary.

steps.title: Close wound and apply post‑op care
steps.instruction: Suture the skin with approximately two sutures posteriorly and two anteriorly, remove the fiber holder and place a protective cap on the fiber, apply a mixture of veterinary wound powder and 0.3 % gentamicin over the sutures and skin, inject 0.5‑1 ml warm sterile saline subcutaneously, and transfer the mouse to the heating pad until it regains locomotion.

substeps.instruction: Move the recovered mouse to its home cage, monitor daily for the first four postoperative days, and house the animal singly.

steps.title: Prepare Super Bond mixture
steps.instruction: In a chilled dispensing dish kept at 4 °C (recommended dish temperature 10‑16 °C), combine one small spoon of polymer L‑type clear, four drops of monomer, and one drop of catalyst; stir gently and apply the mixture with a brush within 2 min of preparation, then clean the dish immediately after use.
